title: Jimmy Noon as idol and influence
summary: Nicholas studied with Noon under Tio, heard him again in Chicago in 1924 and says he and Bigard copied him.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Who were the great clarinetists? Favorites and rivals

blocks.x: Did you hear much of Jimmy Noon in the old days?

I heard Jimmy Noon when I was a kid, 15 years old. As I told you, he was playing with the Young Olympia Band. In fact, we were taking lessons together with Papa Teo also. Jimmy was a couple of, about four years older than I am. And he was playing a lot of clarinet. And it was Jimmy. Bonnie came after me. Bonnie Begarde studied with Teo also. And Omar Simeon in Chicago, studied with Teo. And Teo was in Chicago. Now, Jimmy was one of the best. When he left New Orleans to join Charlie Cook's band. And when we heard him in 24, when I came to Chicago with Bonnie and different ones, when King Oliver sent for us, Jimmy Noon was about the greatest. Because Bonnie and I, every night when we get through playing, when Jimmy was playing in the after our place open around two in the morning. And he was our idol. He had improved so much. And to me, he was the greatest in those days. Yes, I know Jimmy very well. It was a pleasure to hear Jimmy. And of course, I heard him again just before he passed away. He came to New York and he played several times in different places. We copied a lot from Jimmy. Bonnie and I both. We got a lot of
acquaintance from him. Would you say he was a real original?

I should say he was an original. Jimmy Noon was a great musician. And sure, he had his own sound. Because we copied a lot. Benny Goodman's got a lot of things from Jimmy Noon, a lot of guys. The only guy that played different from all of us, I'll be truthful, was Johnny Dodds. He had something different from all of them. I don't think he's taken any lessons. He learned in another way, but it was so beautiful. This guy played a lot of horn, man. He had his own sound, his own fingering and all. I wonder how he did it sometimes. Tone was different. Everything. He was a jazz man, original jazz man.
